blocks.text: Exercise 1. a) Objection: "Some believe that teaching elementary programming is too early." b) Conclusion:               □ I therefore invite the Ministry of Education to include programming in the programmes from next year onwards. □ c) topic (data): Recent studies indicate that children learn logical thinking more easily before the age of ten. d) Introduction: "Lastly there is much talk of the future of education in the age of artificial intelligence." e) Refutation: . However this opinion ignores that today programming is taught by playing, not by equations. f) Theses:          \ And I believe that teaching programming from childhood is no longer a luxury, but a necessity. Exercise 9. a) Introduction: many children come to school knowing of the fuṣḥā Just the cartoons. Thesis: ⁧وأرى أن الحل ليس في منع اللهجة من الصف، بل في استخدامها جسرا نحو الفصحى في السنوات الأولى⁩ ». Topics: pedagogical (the child learns better from what he knows); experience from multilingual countries (data/examples, not named); positive consequences (confidence in itself, participation). Objection: the proposal would threaten the fuṣḥā ( ⁧قد يقال⁩ ). Refutation: the fuṣḥā is in danger of dry teaching, not dialects ( ⁧غير أن⁩ ), with the concession ⁧وإذا كانت الفصحى⁩ … ⁧فإن الطريق إليها⁩ …». Clarification: no books in dialect, no renunciation of the fuṣḥā ( ⁧ولا يعني ذلك⁩ ). Conclusion: dialect as first step; call for a limited and scientifically evaluated trial. ⁧ليس⁩ … ⁧بل⁩ : in the thesis and in the refutation. Connective: ⁧ذلك أن⁩ · ⁧فضلا عن ذلك⁩ · ⁧ومن ثم⁩ · ⁧غير أن⁩ · ⁧خلاصة القول⁩ · ⁧لذا⁩ . The weakest argument: the experiences in several multilingual countries, mentioned without any mention. b) All right: many children have difficulties at first; the teaching of the fuṣḥā be reformed; the child must feel respected; experimentation deserves discussion. Disagreement: on diagnosis and treatment. Topics: fuṣḥā is not foreign to children (stories, songs, TV), the problem is the lack of attractive books; the above mentioned experiences are not mentioned and the Arabic situation is particular (what dialect in a city with children from different regions?); the provisional bridge is likely to become permanent. Weakness highlighted: an argument of unverifiable authority/example (nameless experiences). It accepts limited testing, provided that it is compared with another based on a fuṣḥā simplified from the start. Personal answer in Arabic. Exercise 10. 1. It may be argued that the time is not right for such reforms, but history teaches us that the postponed reforms become more expensive. Delicate points: in 1 no ...so... in 2 the concession with ⁧إلا أن⁩ ; in 3 ⁧ولا يعني ذلك⁩ … ⁧بل⁩ …; in 4 ⁧ومن ثم⁩ and ⁧ليس⁩ … ⁧بل⁩ …; in 5 ⁧قد يقال⁩ as an early objection. Exercise 11.
